title: Settings NOC-row toggle clears overlay_on without view_set_rail — play_w stays rail-shrunk with no rail drawn and D disabled
detail: play_w is manually-synced derived state; this third overlay_on mutation site skips the sync. With D on, toggling the settings row off leaves play_w = win_w − 524: map stays shrunken/left-shifted, no rail drawn, D disabled — only a window resize heals it.
recommended_fix: Call rnd.view_set_rail(&app.view, false) beside overlay_on = false — or better, make view_compute derive play_w from a View-owned rail flag so no call site can forget.

title: Split bottom-band anchor regime: tray keeps win_w centering while the mode label re-anchors to play_w — they collide under D
evidence:
app/render/tray.odin:46-49 (chip rect):
	total_w := f32(i32(n)*cw + (i32(n)-1)*gap)
	x0 := (f32(v.win_w) - total_w) / 2
	return {x0 + f32(i) * f32(cw + gap), f32(v.win_h) - f32(ch) - f32(hud(v, 10)), f32(cw), f32(ch)}
app/main.odin:1600:
	draw_text(app, mode_label, app.view.play_w - rnd.hud(&app.view, 320), app.view.win_h - rnd.hud(&app.view, 24), rnd.hud(&app.view, 15), p.ink_soft_text)
detail: At 1280×720 the tray is 6 chips (3 pipe_tiers + 3 junction node_types) = 616px, x0=332..948, y 684..710; rail starts at x=756. With D on the label anchors at 436 — on top of tray chips — and the tray's last two chips paint over the rail's drop-log rows.
recommended_fix: Pick one bottom-band policy: center the tray on play_w (tray_chip_rect) and right-anchor the mode label to play_w minus its measured width so label, tray and rail never collide.

title: Generic View state hardcodes the NOC overlay's geometry — view.odin's view_set_rail binds to NOC_RAIL_W
detail: View/camera state (win_w/play_w/scale) is surface-agnostic everywhere else, but the playfield concept is now welded to one panel's constant. A second docked surface would need another flag and another sync site.
recommended_fix: Pass the dock width in (view_set_rail(v, on, rail_w)) or store rail state on View and derive play_w inside view_compute — keeping view.odin free of NOC names.

title: NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE is disconnected from NOC_PANEL_W — the documented 'tunable' changes nothing
evidence:
app/render/noc_overlay.odin:332-333:
NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE :: 1.4            // the panel-width scale (the ruling)
NOC_PANEL_W       :: 360 * 14 / 10 // 504 (= 360 × NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE, exact int math) — the rail width
grep over app/ harness/ *.odin: NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE appears only in this definition, its comment, and a test comment — never in an expression.
detail: Hard rule 2 names the panel-width scale as a tunable, but the width hardcodes 360*14/10; editing the scale constant silently does nothing while comments and tests claim it is the derivation.
recommended_fix: Derive the width from the scale in integer math, e.g. NOC_PANEL_W :: 360 * NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE_PERMILLE / 1000 with NOC_PANEL_W_SCALE_PERMILLE :: 1400, or delete the dead constant.

title: Rail content-column left edge derived twice — noc_panel_x vs noc_panel_rect().x + NOC_PLATE_PAD
detail: Two independent formulas for the same edge; they agree only through the RAIL_W constant identity. This is the exact derivation-drift class the codebase fixed before (camera_fit, 'Perkins r2 N1 — the fit was triplicated').
recommended_fix: Define noc_panel_x as i32(noc_panel_rect(win_w, 0).x) + NOC_PLATE_PAD so the plate rect is the single geometry source.
